title: PVT Properties of Concentrated Aqueous Electrolytes. 7. The Volumes of Mixing of the Reciprocal Salt Pairs KCl, K2SO4, NaCl, and Na2SO4 at 25 C and I = 1.5 m
experimental_method: Picker vibrating-flow densimeter at 25 C (thermostat +-0.001 C), calibrated with water and seawater; solutions made by weight, stock molalities checked from density.
uncertainties_stated: Standard errors of the mixing-volume fits given as density errors of 1e-6 to 8e-6 g/cm3 (Table II, not extracted); density measurement precision not otherwise stated for Table I.
quality_remarks: Temperature on IPTS-68. Pressure not stated. Relative densities Delta rho = rho - rho0 with rho0 taken as pure-water density (reference not further specified). Ionic-strength fraction y3 as the composition measure; the pure end points (y3 = 0 and 1.0) of different pairs are repeated and differ slightly. The text layer printed y3 = 0 as '5' for the first row; the image shows 0.
needs_pass2_reason: All 61 Delta rho values and y3 values were read from the page image and agree with the text layer numbers (only the y3 = 0 glyph of the first row was garbled in the text layer, and that was never used).
not_extracted_tables: Table II: parameters v0, v1 of the mixing-volume equation (model parameters)
Table III: verification of the cross-square rule (derived mixing volumes)
Table IV (journal p. 472): maximum errors in density of the Wood-Reilly equation (model comparison, derived)

Table I.printed: 61 data rows in 6 mixture blocks (+6 label rows)

extraction_notes: Label rows written for each mixture; the mixture name printed beside the first data row was split into its own label row. Sanity: within each block Delta rho varies smoothly between the end points.
